findings: All 48 positive descriptions preserve the selected task-defining operation, objective and result; omitted incidental numeric bounds do not change semantic identity. They are not full input validators.

All 24 contrasts change a real selected-contract requirement: optimization direction, contiguity, multiplicity, empty selection, tie-break, swap locality, refill policy, rearrangement, exact cardinality, operation order, encoding width, strict inequality, per-hour work sharing, padding, graph direction, resource equality, distinct-value cardinality, distance objective, adjacency, vertex deletion, prefix strictness or balanced order. They are not catalogue-wide absence labels.

No task ID, URL, benchmark label or explicit title identifier is embedded in the description strings. Natural task vocabulary overlaps statements by design; this is not guaranteed unfamiliar-task testing.

Every span exactly matches its Unicode-code-point offsets. The domain/objective/output segments are sensible coarse rhetorical roles, not mutually exclusive semantic atoms. Some extrema/cardinality requirements occur in output segments and some operation restrictions occur in domain segments.

All three 1515 rows retain unresolved_scope_limited and delivery-ineligible flags; its two semantic positives do not establish general artifact applicability beyond the recorded 20-fixture analytic family. Other 69 rows retain unevaluated applicability.

Selection order and exclusion disjointness verified on the frozen selected list. First-24 completeness among the asserted 128 eligible rows was not recomputed because the broader catalogue was not reopened.
